page: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-14-standardlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The configuration allocates 14 dedicated vCPUs spanning 7 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, accompanied by a 105 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning stands at 112 GB, creating an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio suited for large working sets. Storage is directly integrated via a bundled 3,221 GB local NVMe SSD, offering low-latency physical disk access without external network attachments. The instance operates without discrete GPU acceleration and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance across testing suites demonstrates mid-tier output relative to its resource bracket. Benchmark results place its multi-core CPU capacity at 11,635.06 in stress-ng and 9,436.0 in Geekbench multi-core testing. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 85.51 GB/s, while write bandwidth sustains 39.89 GB/s. For in-memory database operations, the instance records 15.53 million Redis SET operations per second. Modern hardware acceleration extensions are supported, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX-TILE, AMX-INT8) and AVX-512, which provide computational efficiency for vectorized mathematics and inference tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance targets environments that require both substantial RAM capacity and attached NVMe storage, removing the need to provision independent high-throughput block storage volumes. However, workloads requiring persistent disk endurance beyond the host lifecycle must account for the ephemeral nature of local SSDs. The z3-highmem-14-standardlssd is best aligned with transactional relational databases, NoSQL engines, distributed caching clusters, search indexes, and high-throughput data ingestion pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-14-standardlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine configured with 14 dedicated vCPUs across 7 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance delivers 112 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 gigabyte-to-vCPU allocation, and includes a bundled 3,221 GB local NVMe SSD. Architecturally based on x86_64, the CPU integrates hardware acceleration technologies such as Intel AMX and AVX-512 vector extensions. Benchmark results locate the instance consistently within the middle 50 percent range, achieving 15.53 million Redis SET operations per second and 85.51 GB/s uncached read memory bandwidth. Lacking dedicated GPUs and standard complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance balances hardware cost efficiency by packaging high memory density alongside large-capacity local NVMe storage. This architectural profile is designed for input-output intensive workloads, including distributed transactional databases, persistent caching clusters, real-time analytics, and data pipeline processing requiring fast temporary scratch space.
